subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — retries blowing up throughput
messages:
From: J. Carter <ops@lumenhealth.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <eng-lead@lumenhealth.com>, Mark D. <ceo@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T08:15:00Z
Subject: Production errors — spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts

Dylan,

We're seeing a production incident starting ~08:05 UTC: sudden increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood endpoint. Our frontend is seeing widespread timeouts and the system is effectively degraded. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side — no deploys, same SDK version (internal wrapper around your JS SDK).

Attached: a short trace of several failed requests (request IDs) and a small log snippet.

What we see: 500/502/504 and application-level 429s. Error percentage jumping from ~0.2% to ~18% in under 3 minutes. Retries from the client appear aggressive; many requests show 3-5 quick re-attempts within seconds.

This is impacting our CarePaths product in US-east. We need immediate mitigation (rate reduction, advice to stop retries, or anything urgent) and an ETA for permanent fix. We are escalating internally as well.

-Jason Carter
Ops Lead, LumenHealth

Attachments: request_trace_20270303.txt, svc_logs_snippet.gz
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: J. Carter <ops@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <eng-lead@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Production errors — spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts

Jason — thanks for the fast heads-up and the traces. We're looking at this now. Two immediate asks while we investigate:

1) If you can temporarily disable client retries in your wrapper (or set retry count to 0) that will likely reduce amplification immediately.
2) Can you confirm whether your wrapper overrides SDK exponential backoff with a fixed interval? That pattern often removes jitter and causes synchronized retries.

I'm looping in our on-call engineering and platform leads (cc'd). I'll follow up in 10–15 mins with mitigation steps we can push from our side (throttles, short-term model downgrade, or routing).

—Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <eng-lead@lumenhealth.com>, J. Carter <ops@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T08:30:00Z
Subject: URGENT: LumenHealth production spike — suspected client retry amplification

Team — LumenHealth (LH-4763) reports a rapid jump in 5xx/429 starting ~08:05 UTC. Customer traces show multiple tight retries from their wrapper. Quick summary of telemetry:
- Error rate: baseline ~0.2% -> peak ~18% for 08:05–08:20 UTC
- Affected region: us-east (primary)
- Top symptom: many short-interval retry bursts (3–6 attempts within <10s) per request
- Impact: frontend timeouts, increased queueing on inference runtime, elevated latencies for other customers behind same pool

Attachments: svc_logs_snippet.gz (server side errors), request_trace_20270303.txt (customer trace).

Immediate asks:
- Can Platform apply a short-term per-customer token rate-limit (soft throttle) or lower concurrency for LH to reduce pressure?
- Engineering: Can we push a temporary model variant that is lighter (degrade quality) to free capacity?
- SDK/Product: we need to confirm if our public SDK default retries / backoff are safe and if LH's wrapper overrides them.

I propose we: (A) tell customer to disable retries for 30 minutes, (B) apply per-customer throttle to keep failures contained, (C) release a targeted SDK patch if their wrapper is observable as malformed.

I will coordinate comms to LumenHealth and provide an ETA.

—Dylan
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <eng-lead@lumenhealth.com>, J. Carter <ops@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: LumenHealth production spike — suspected client retry amplification

Thanks — quick findings from runtime team (summary):
- Root cause: customer wrapper had removed jitter and set retry count to 6 with a fixed 500ms interval. Combined with a transient 502 from a single worker, that caused massively synchronized retry waves.
- Our logs show a spike in connection attempts to the same worker and rising queue depth; backlog pushed request processing time from ~60ms to ~480ms which led to more client-side timeouts and retries — feedback loop.

Mitigation already applied (09:00–09:12 UTC):
1) Temporary per-token soft throttle for LH: limited to 60 QPS (was unlimited); this immediately reduced incoming request bursts.
2) Fallback routing: 15% of LH traffic routed to a lower-cost model variant (faster, slightly lower quality) to reduce average token compute time.
3) Enabled circuit-breaker on the affected worker group to avoid repeated attempts to the same failing hosts.

Next steps (ETA):
- Customer action: ask LH to disable client retries or set retry count=0 and re-enable jitter (immediate) — Dylan to confirm.
- SDK/Product: we'll ship a 1.2.3 patch within 24 hrs that enforces jitter and caps default retries at 2 (unless explicitly overridden). QA and release pipelines are queued.
- Postmortem: we'll run a root-cause review and propose default SDK settings and a short KB for customers about safe retry patterns.

I'll take the lead on the patch; Laura and Vivek please confirm rollout window for dedicated pools and whether we need a hotfix for any pinned infra config.

—Marissa
Sr. Eng Manager, Runtime

Date: 2027-03-05T16:42:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors — spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts — mitigation & next steps

Jason / Priya — thanks again for patience. Summary and plan:

What happened:
- A transient 502 on a worker triggered tight, synchronous retries from LumenHealth's internal wrapper. Their wrapper had disabled jitter and set retry count to 6 with a fixed 500ms delay. The combination created a retry storm that amplified errors and caused downstream latency increases.

What we did (immediate):
- Advised LH to disable client retries (they confirmed at 08:28 UTC).
- Applied soft per-token throttle (60 QPS) while we stabilized.
- Routed 15% of traffic to a faster, lower-cost model variant to reduce compute pressure.
- Enabled worker circuit-breaker to avoid retrying the same failed hosts.

Planned (short-term):
- SDK release 1.2.3 (within 24 hrs of detection): default max retries = 2, exponential backoff with randomized jitter enabled by default, and a clear opt-out flag.
- KB: "Safe retry patterns for Redwood clients" to be published to support.redwood.ai (by EOD+2).
- Postmortem: Platform + Runtime + Product to produce RCA and recommended defaults (by EOD+7).

Longer term:
- Add server-side throttles and adaptive queuing policies per-account to avoid single-customer storms affecting shared pools.
- Consider exposing a per-customer retry-protection flag customers can opt into (server-side advisory that reduces retries automatically).

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook we used for this incident).

If you want a short call to walk through the changes and the SDK patch timeline, we can set one up today.

—Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
